sections.h2: How can you sell a house fast in Orland Park?
sections.html:
Orland Park sellers have three practical routes: a traditional listing, a sale without an agent, or a direct cash purchase. A cash buyer can close the fastest, while a listing often brings the highest price for a house in good order.

Orland Park is a village 25 miles southwest of Chicago, and most of it lies in Cook County with a small piece in Will County. Population is 57,954. Most of the present housing arrived after 1960, and owners live in 85.8% of homes.

  • List with an agent when the roof, furnace and kitchen are in decent shape and you can wait through showings and a buyer's mortgage approval.
  • Sell it yourself when you are comfortable negotiating and coordinating with a title company and the village.
  • Take a cash offer when the house needs repairs, a probate is pending, or a tenant must be dealt with. Compare it against a listing price less commission, repairs and months of carrying costs.

sections.h2: Registering a rental before a sale
sections.html:
The village runs a rental registration program, and it applies to single-family homes, townhomes and condominiums as well as apartment buildings. The annual fee is $100 per unit for a detached or attached single-family residence and $100 plus $15 per additional unit for a multi-family building.

  • Inspections follow the village's tri-annual schedule, and a rental housing sticker is issued when the unit passes.
  • Landlords or their agents must attend one eight-hour Crime Free Housing seminar from the police department.
  • Every lease must carry the village's Crime Free Lease Addendum, signed by each tenant age 18 or older.

When a rental is part of the sale, tell the buyer whether the unit is registered and when the last inspection took place. Development Services answers registration questions at (708) 403-5300.

sections.h2: Water service and the private line
sections.html:
The village bills water every two months, and a high bill should be reviewed by calling 708-403-6175. Property owners are responsible for the private water line from the shut-off valve, usually in the parkway, to the house, plus any leaks inside.

If a buyer's inspection finds a leak on that line, the repair is yours to make or to credit. Check the meter and the line before you list, and keep the bill history to show that the usage is normal. A buyer who sees a clean history is less likely to ask for a credit, and a cash buyer will usually take the line as it is.

sections.h2: How do Cook County taxes work for an Orland Park sale?
sections.html:
Property tax comes from Cook County. Orland Township is in the 2023 and 2026 reassessment group, and the township assessor's office is at 14807 S. Ravinia Ave., phone (708) 403-4222. Cook County bills in two installments, so ask the Treasurer for the next due dates and for a copy of your bill. Then ask your closing agent how the year's tax is prorated between you and the buyer.

A small part of Orland Park lies in Will County. If your house is in that part, ask the Will County treasurer for the schedule on your bill. Check the county named on your tax bill before you call, so you reach the right office.

sections.h2: Steps for an Orland Park seller
sections.html:
Selling a house in Orland Park comes down to a short sequence, and doing it in order saves time.

  1. Decide whether the house is a good candidate for a listing or whether repairs, a probate or a tenant point toward a cash sale.
  2. If a tenant lives there, check that the unit is registered with the village and gather the inspection sticker and the signed Crime Free Lease Addendum.
  3. Walk the water line from the shut-off valve in the parkway to the house, and look for leaks inside.
  4. Find your tax bill, note whether it comes from Cook County or Will County, and call the right treasurer for the schedule.
  5. Ask your title company about village charges and get them in writing before the closing date.
  6. Confirm the school boundary for your street so your listing sheet is correct.

A cash buyer takes the house as it stands, so you skip the repair requests that follow a buyer's inspection, and the wait for a lender's approval. A listing gives you more time on the market and a chance at a higher price, but the same village paperwork applies either way.

sections.h2: Parks and neighborhood features buyers ask about
sections.html:
Buyers mostly ask about parks, shopping and the village's recreation facilities. The village lists more than 60 parks, and Centennial Park holds the Aquatic Center with six water slides, Lake Sedgwick with boardwalks and pedal boats, and a free outdoor ice rink that runs from November to March. The Sportsplex on 159th Street is the largest indoor recreation building.

Shopping centers include Orland Square Mall and Orland Park Crossing. A listing that names the nearest park and shopping center gives a buyer something concrete to picture.

Most of the Cook County part of Orland Park is in Orland School District 135, and all of it feeds Consolidated High School District 230, whose Carl Sandburg High School serves most of the village. Addresses in the northern edge may instead be zoned to Stagg or Victor J. Andrew high schools, so confirm the exact school for your street.

Four elementary districts reach Orland Park in Cook County: District 135, Community Consolidated District 146, Palos District 118 and Kirby District 140. In Will County, Mokena School District 159 and Lincoln-Way Community High School District 210 cover homes in the village. A listing that names the nearest park, Metra station and school boundary answers the questions buyers raise first.

Ask the village finance office and your title company which village charges apply to your closing, and get the figures in writing before the closing date. Cook County reassesses each township every three years, so a new notice arrives in the reassessment year and the township assessor can answer questions about it.

Metra's SouthWest Service stops at 143rd Street, 153rd Street and 179th Street, and Interstate 80 forms the southern edge of the village. Commuters like both, so mention the distance to the nearest station in your listing, along with the main roads: La Grange Road, 159th Street and Harlem Avenue.

faqs.q: Does Orland Park charge a transfer tax when I sell?
faqs.a: Ask the village finance office and your title company which village charges apply to your closing, and get the figures in writing before the closing date.

faqs.q: Which county bills property tax in Orland Park?
faqs.a: Cook County, for almost all of the village. A small part sits in Will County and is billed there. Check the county named on your tax bill.

faqs.q: Do I have to register a rental house in Orland Park before selling it?
faqs.a: If it is rented, yes, the village requires annual registration at $100 per unit for a single-family home, with inspections on a tri-annual schedule. Share the registration and inspection records with the buyer.

faqs.q: Where do I report a high final water bill in Orland Park?
faqs.a: Call the village water billing line at 708-403-6175. The village bills two months at a time, and owners are responsible for leaks on the private line and inside the house.

faqs.q: How is Orland Park's reassessment schedule set?
faqs.a: Cook County reassesses each township every three years. Orland Township is in the 2023 and 2026 group, so a new notice arrives in the reassessment year and the township assessor can answer questions.
